Maya (Support): Hey team, customer reports a spike of 502s for Hosted API during a model swap this morning. They say it started right when we rolled v12 -> v13 for the `text-gen-large` family. Sample request id: req_0a1b2c3d. They can repro consistently when the deployment happens.
Ashok (Eng-SRE): Got it — can you paste the customer's curl + headers and the exact timestamp? Also any trace ids?
Maya (Support): Timestamp 2026-03-16T08:43:12Z (approx). Curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` . They included upstream trace: `trace=trc-7f8e9a` and the edge request id above.
Samir (DevEx): Quick theory: model swap triggers backend capacity pressure (warmup / weight load), upstreams stop accepting new streams and envoy returns 502 from cluster. Possible connection pool exhaustion or LB health drain.
Ops Oncall: I pulled the edge logs for req_0a1b2c3d — see snippet.
Infra Bot: ```
[08:43:12.234] edge-proxy WARN request=req_0a1b2c3d upstream=nginx-upstream-23 status=502 reason="upstream connect error or disconnect"
[08:43:12.235] envoy ERROR stream reset: rst_code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM downstream=conn-45 upstream=conn-129
[08:43:12.236] upstream-health INFO host=10.12.8.45 state=unhealthy check-failures=3
```
Ashok (Eng-SRE): That aligns. During the rollout we saw a short window where many backends reported health checks failing (weight load cpu spike). Envoy then started answering 502s as cluster became drained.
Maya (Support): Customer asked if we have graceful fallbacks (smaller model variant or cached last-good) instead of 502s. They rely on low-latency.
Samir (DevEx): We do have fallback policies but not always enabled for model swaps. Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) Enable model-variant fallback (route to `text-gen-medium` when `text-gen-large` pool < 50% healthy). 2) Increase upstream connection pool / keepalive on edge for short-term. 3) Pause rollout or do canary with traffic shifting.
Ashok (Eng-SRE): For the current incident I recommend: rollback v13 to v12, mark hosts as draining gradually, and enable `graceful_degrade` routing flag for that customer tenant while we patch rollout automation. I'll open a quick rollback PR.
Ops Oncall: Doing rollback now. Noted that kube pods for model v13 were OOMing during weight init on some hosts — need to limit concurrency of weight loads.
Maya (Support): I've informed the customer and asked for patience. They requested repro steps — here's the minimal repro they shared: 1) hit production endpoint repeatedly during a rolling deploy of model, 2) use concurrent 20 connections with small payloads, 3) observe ~10-20% 502s for ~30s window.
Samir (DevEx): Can you capture a client-side `curl --trace-ascii` + server edge request id next time. We should add a short-runplaybook in docs: tune `max_concurrent_weight_loads` and enable `model-fallback` in rollout manifest.
Ashok (Eng-SRE): Action items: (a) rollback done (pod counts back to 95% healthy), (b) increase envoy upstream max-conns by 30% in canary pool, (c) add healthcheck grace window during weight loads, (d) ticket to add auto-fallback routing. I'll paste PR and ticket ids shortly.
Maya (Support): PR and ticket would be great. Customer is OK with canary + fallback if we provide timeline. Thanks. :thumbsup:
Infra Bot: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rollout/PR-4821, Ticket: INF-7082
Ashok (Eng-SRE): Follow-up note — longer term we should: bake warm pools for model swaps or stream weights lazily per-request with backpressure; both reduce mass unhealthy transitions.
Maya (Support): Filing a support follow-up to the customer with the mitigation steps and ETA. Closing thread once tickets are created.
